purpose: Deterministic, graph-conditioned teaching spectra. Generate reusable band envelopes and chemically justified fingerprint structure, not stored molecular polylines.

calibration.ir: The supplied traces support qualitative shapes, approximate positions, relative prominence, and selected environment contrasts. They do not establish universal experimental intensities or exact peak positions.
calibration.nmr: No NMR traces or peak lists were supplied. All 1H/13C shifts and coupling rules below are textbook priors, not measurements extracted from these IR traces.
calibration.default_conditions: Condensed-phase, hydrogen-bonded IR; room-temperature NMR in an achiral solvent with rapid ordinary bond rotation and rapidly exchanging OH protons.
calibration.output_claim: Exam-quality schematic prediction, not a reconstructed or guaranteed experimental spectrum.

units.Tmin: percent transmittance for an isolated, single-instance template

validation: Parse and sanitize SMILES with explicit bond orders, formal charges, isotope labels, and supplied stereochemistry.
Reject any aromatic atom or aromatic bond.
Reject any molecular cycle, including non-aromatic rings.
Require one connected molecular component for the default generator; mixtures and salts require an explicit mixture or ionic-species model.
Do not interpret acyclic non-aromatic as necessarily saturated.
motif_precedence: Identify complete functional groups before assigning individual bond templates.
Classify each carbonyl once: carboxylic acid, ester, other acyl derivative, aldehyde, or ketone.
A neutral carboxylic acid requires C(=O)-O-H. C(=O)-O-C is an ester, not an acid.
Alcohol OH requires O-H attached to an sp3 carbon. Acid OH must not also produce an alcohol template.
Primary and secondary alcohol classes use the number of carbon neighbors of the OH-bearing carbon: one and two, respectively.
Methanol and tertiary alcohols require their own environment handling; neither should be silently forced into a CH2OH or CHOH template.
Alkyl bromide requires an sp3 C-Br bond. Acyl bromides are not alkyl bromides.
canonicalization.invariance: Use canonical graph descriptors and motif counts, never input atom order, SMILES character positions, molecule names, or a molecule-specific random seed.

coverage.supported: Alkane skeletons and new saturated, neutral combinations of the seven listed functional-group families.
coverage.conditional: Strongly interacting adjacent functional groups, unusual steric environments, and intramolecular hydrogen bonding receive wider uncertainty intervals.
coverage.unsupported_policy: Unrepresented chemistry requires an explicitly versioned textbook-prior extension. Otherwise return the recognized features with status incomplete and list unsupported environments. Never present a partial spectrum as complete.

primitives.compact_support: For narrow-band primitives, multiply by a smooth window equal to 1 within 3 widths of the center, falling by a cosine taper to 0 at 4 widths. This prevents unphysical long tails.
primitives.normalization: After constructing and windowing a band or cluster, divide its profile by its maximum. Profiles are nonnegative.

P.description: Compact pseudo-Voigt peak for resolved stretches, bends, and rocking modes.

G.description: Smooth broader Gaussian feature for unresolved deformation envelopes.

S.description: Sharp, deep carbonyl core with a restrained broader skirt.
S.width_definition: FWHM parameter of the narrow core, not the total composite.
S.formula: Normalize 0.85*P0(nu; nu0, width) + 0.15*G(nu; nu0, 3*width), with compact support applied to each component.
S.note: The skirt is not a second carbonyl and must not become a broad, deep feature near 1900 cm^-1.

A.description: Smooth asymmetric hydrogen-bonded alcohol OH envelope.
A.width_definition: Nominal FWHM; low_scale + high_scale = 2 before support tapering.
A.formula: Use exp(-4*ln(2)*((nu-nu0)/(width*s))^2), with s=low_scale below nu0 and s=high_scale above nu0.
A.window: Use smooth cosine transitions between the support edges and full-window edges.
A.note: One continuous envelope, not a comb of narrow OH peaks. The upper onset may extend slightly above 3600, but it is smooth.

C.description: Carboxylic-acid OH canyon: very broad, asymmetric, and shouldered, with alkyl CH peaks superimposed separately.
C.width_definition: Overall envelope scale, not a single-peak FWHM.
C.window: Smooth cosine transitions at both ends.
C.note: The overlapping broad components describe a canyon, not three assigned OH fundamentals. Weak acid-specific shoulders are allowed; random ripples are not.

M.description: Small coupled-mode cluster with graph-conditioned component positions and weights.
M.formula: Normalize the sum over components of weight_i*P(nu; nu0+offset_i, width*width_factor_i).
M.note: Two or three meaningful components are preferred to a dense comb. Components describe a reusable motif, not copied local minima.

formula: For each active band j, a_j = -log10(Tmin_j/98).
Construct its normalized nonnegative shape phi_j(nu).
Combine identical environment templates using count scaling rather than cloning an entire spectrum.
rendering.count_scale: For n>=1, min(1.8, 1+0.25*ln(n)); emit nothing for n=0. This is a bounded teaching-spectrum prominence rule, not a Beer-Lambert concentration calibration.
rendering.overlap: Add absorbance, not transmittance dips. Actual rendered minima may be lower than isolated-band Tmin values.
rendering.baseline_policy: Flat high-transmittance baseline outside assigned envelopes; no synthetic baseline waviness or random noise.
rendering.high_frequency_policy: Above about 3600 cm^-1, permit only the smooth upper onset of an applicable OH envelope. No unrelated isolated peaks or jagged structure.
rendering.plot_policy: Plot wavenumber decreasing from left to right. Use non-overshooting interpolation if a coarser exported curve is needed.
output_metadata: IR curve generated from the active parameters

shared_ir_rules.when: At least one saturated carbon bearing three H
shared_ir_rules.note: Count methyl environments; do not add one peak per C-H bond.

shared_ir_rules.when: At least one saturated carbon bearing two H

shared_ir_rules.note: For an acyl CH3 use approximately 1370 and Tmin 40. For an isopropyl motif, replace its contribution with the branched-methyl pair.

shared_ir_rules.when: A carbon bearing H is attached to two CH3 groups
shared_ir_rules.note: A characteristic coupled methyl-deformation pattern; do not duplicate the same methyl groups in the ordinary symmetric-deformation band.

shared_ir_rules.when: A CH2 participates in a C-C-C path or is directly attached to O, Br, or a carbonyl carbon
shared_ir_rules.note: Weak, approximate fingerprint support. A more specific overlapping motif replaces this contribution rather than being duplicated.

shared_ir_rules.when: At least one saturated C-C-C path
shared_ir_rules.note: Low-confidence skeletal support. Suppress if already represented by an overlapping C-O or specific skeletal cluster.
Weak representative fingerprint feature, not a universal exact 970 cm^-1 diagnostic.

shared_ir_rules.when: At least three consecutive CH2 carbons
shared_ir_rules.note: Typical range roughly 720-750; chain conformation can alter visibility.

shared_ir_rules.when: At least one saturated C-C-C path
shared_ir_rules.note: Restrained broad skeletal structure, not a molecular identification claim.

bands.note: Broad hydrogen-bonded OH. The ethanol/propan-1-ol difference does not justify a fixed OH frequency increment per added carbon.
Reusable split C-O/coupled skeletal cluster near 1030-1090, rather than one generic alcohol Gaussian.
Moderate, unresolved fingerprint contribution.

bands.when: The CH2OH group terminates a carbon chain containing at least three carbons
bands.note: A motif-level extension suggested by propan-1-ol; not a copied propan-1-ol fingerprint.

primary_alcohol.fpr: Combine the split C-O cluster, applicable CH2/CH3 bends near 1465/1450/1380, and a small number of activated skeletal modes. Do not transfer the ethanol 895 cm^-1 notch or propan-1-ol low-frequency spikes to every primary alcohol.

bands.note: Same broad OH shape family as primary alcohols; the robust distinction is primarily in the C-O region and carbon skeleton.
Higher-frequency C-O/coupled-mode cluster than the primary-alcohol template; typical useful envelope is about 1090-1170.
Moderate coupled skeletal support. The very deep 954 cm^-1 feature in 2-propanol is not a universal secondary-alcohol requirement.

secondary_alcohol.fpr: Use the shifted C-O cluster and graph-selected bends. Activate the 1365/1385 branched-methyl pair only when the actual substitution pattern warrants it.

bands.note: Broad approximately 2500-3500 OH absorption under the ordinary CH stretches. Default assumes associated neutral acid.
Strong narrow carbonyl core within a modest skirt; ordinary saturated-acid expectation approximately 1700-1725.
C-O/OH-coupled fingerprint region; component weights and center are adjusted by the alpha-carbon environment.
Overlaps ordinary alkyl deformations.
Associated-acid OH out-of-plane envelope around 900-950. This is not aromatic out-of-plane absorption.

carboxylic_acid.fpr: Require the carbonyl spike, acid OH canyon, structured C-O region, and associated-acid approximately 930 envelope. Distinguish acetic and propanoic acids using alpha-CH3 versus alpha-CH2 and the resulting alkyl/coupled-mode pattern.

bands.note: Saturated acyclic ketone default; approximate range 1705-1725.

bands.when: A CH3 is directly bonded to the ketone carbonyl carbon
bands.note: Acetone supports a prominent acyl-skeletal fingerprint feature here. Do not label it C-O single-bond stretching.
Weak low-frequency skeleton envelope, not a copied 531 cm^-1 line.

ketone.fpr: Strong carbonyl, acyl-alkyl bending structure, and restrained skeleton bands. No OH envelope and no aldehyde Fermi pair.

bands.note: Textbook-corrected saturated-aldehyde default, approximately 1720-1740. Do not establish 1710 as universal from the supplied trace.
Textbook prior; not convincingly resolved in the supplied propionaldehyde trace. Can be weak or absent experimentally.
May overlap the low-frequency edge of ordinary CH stretching.

bands.when: An alkyl substituent is attached to CHO
bands.note: Weak representative fingerprint support; exact position is low confidence.

aldehyde.fpr: Carbonyl plus weak aldehydic CH features and graph-derived alkyl bends. Do not reproduce the anomalous approximately 3130 or 1580 features as universal saturated-aldehyde diagnostics.

bands.note: Saturated acyclic ester default; approximate range 1730-1750.
Strong coupled C-O region, with environment uncertainty across approximately 1180-1300.
Lower-frequency coupled C-O structure. Alkoxy substitution may change positions and relative intensities; one ethyl ester does not calibrate all esters.

bands.when: The ester alkoxy side contains an O-CH2-C path
bands.note: Moderate support only; do not force ethyl acetate's deep 939/917 doublet onto every ester.

ester.fpr: Strong carbonyl plus at least two differentiated C-O-region contributions and applicable alkyl bends. An ester oxygen does not create OH.

bands.note: Representative C-Br band; substantial environment uncertainty across roughly 500-650. The supplied primary bromide does not establish a universal substitution-dependent frequency law.

bands.when: An sp3 CH2-Br group is present
bands.note: Coupled deformation; replaces the overlapping generic wag contribution for this environment.

alkyl_bromide.fpr: Alkyl stretching and bending pattern, CH2Br deformation when applicable, chain-dependent rocking, and low-frequency C-Br absorption. Do not duplicate the entire bromobutane fingerprint for other bromoalkanes.

environment_rules: For acids define alpha as the carbon directly bonded to the carboxyl carbon. In acetic acid it is CH3; in propanoic acid it is CH2. Do not classify these by total molecular carbon count alone.
For an acid with alpha-CH3, retain the 1290-centered C-O cluster and use the stronger acyl-CH3 deformation near 1370. There is no alpha-CH2 scissor or wag.

For an acid with alpha-CH2, use an illustrative acid C-O cluster centered at 1250 with components at offsets -70, 0, and +40, weights 0.5, 1, and 0.45, and reference width 34. Activate CH2 scissoring/wagging and retain any terminal-CH3 bends elsewhere in the molecule.
The acid alpha-CH2 versus alpha-CH3 C-O adjustment is a low-confidence motif-level generalization from these two traces, not a universal 40 cm^-1 law. Do not impose a comparably large carbonyl shift.

For primary alcohols, a CH2 rather than CH3 at the beta carbon favors the upper portion of the primary C-O cluster. A canonical option is nu0 1060 with offsets -15 and +15 and weights 0.7 and 1. Keep the shift small and uncertainty explicit.

Secondary alcohols use the approximately 1100-1165 C-O cluster even when the molecule has the same formula as a primary alcohol. Their complete fingerprints still depend on their actual carbon skeletons.

Generate one shared alcohol OH envelope for a polyol, not one separated broad trough per OH. For two or more alcohol OH groups use a canonical nu0 of 3340 and width min(520, 420+30*(nOH-1)), with bounded count scaling.

For polyols retain the applicable primary and secondary C-O motifs, combining overlapping contributions in absorbance. Glycerol therefore has both primary and secondary C-O character, but no carbonyl.
Do not infer that more OH groups necessarily shifts the OH maximum upward. The unusual high-frequency glycerol plateau is not a universal polyol rule.
For hydroxy acids combine the acid canyon and alcohol contribution without inventing multiple resolved OH maxima. Keep the acid carbonyl and acid out-of-plane band.
The common 1450/1465 and 1380 region is populated only by present CH classes. Methine-only or methyl-free structures must not receive a fictitious methyl bend.
Acyl-CH3 deformation intensity can be enhanced in ketones, esters, and acids. An alkoxy methyl in an ester is not an acyl methyl.
An alkyl bromide receives no OH, carbonyl, or C-O diagnostic solely because bromobutane has fingerprint bands in those regions.
Only actual repeated motifs increase template prominence. Chain length may add eligible CH2 and skeletal motifs, but must not trigger uniform spectral roughness.

Conjugation with an alkene commonly lowers carbonyl frequency, but it requires an explicit unsaturated-environment extension. Do not apply an isolated saturated-carbonyl prediction to an unrecognized conjugated system.
Carbonyls adjacent to additional heteroatoms, multiple carbonyls, or unusual substituents require a composite rule or wider uncertainty, not unlimited additive frequency increments.

equivalence: Build environments from the molecular graph, not from SMILES substrings or shift-bin names.
For 13C, determine carbon equivalence under molecular symmetry with the supplied stereochemistry and the declared rapid-motion assumptions.

For 1H, include attached hydrogens, methyl rotational averaging, symmetry, and stereotopicity analysis. Use a substitution test where necessary to distinguish homotopic, enantiotopic, and diastereotopic hydrogens.
Homotopic and, in the default achiral medium, enantiotopic sites share a chemical shift. Diastereotopic CH2 hydrogens can require separate resonances and geminal coupling.
Identical shift-bin assignments do not prove equivalence. Keep distinct environment IDs even when their representative ppm values coincide.
Unspecified relative stereochemistry may make the number or position of resonances ambiguous. Report that ambiguity instead of choosing a hidden stereoisomer.
nmr_equivalence_and_rendering.integration: 1H integration equals the number of hydrogens in the chemical-equivalence class. OH/COOH integrations are nominal because exchange can affect experimental integrals.
multiplicity: Use n+1 only for an approximately first-order signal coupled to one set of n equivalent spin-1/2 neighbors with a common J.
For distinct neighbor sets, use the product of their individual splittings and report labels such as triplet of quartets rather than automatically summing all neighbors.
Equivalent protons do not split one another in the elementary first-order treatment.
Equal or unresolved J values may collapse a product pattern to an apparent simpler multiplet; label this as apparent.
Use a default alkyl vicinal J prior of about 7 Hz only for a schematic rendering, with a typical 5-9 Hz uncertainty interval.
Aldehyde-to-alpha-proton coupling is often small, approximately 1-3 Hz; do not omit it merely because CHO has its own shift bin.
Rapidly exchanging OH and COOH are broad singlets by default and do not split adjacent CH signals.
Diastereotopic CH2 systems, magnetic nonequivalence, or small frequency separation relative to J require a complex/multiplet label or spin-system calculation, not a forced n+1 answer.
nmr_equivalence_and_rendering.carbon_spectrum: Default 13C output is broadband 1H-decoupled: one singlet per distinct carbon environment. Carbon counts are annotations, not quantitative peak heights.
nmr_equivalence_and_rendering.shift_selection: Apply the most specific complete environment bin before generic CH3, CH2, or CH bins. Use explicit composite bins for competing strong effects.
nmr_equivalence_and_rendering.precision: Representative shifts are deliberately coarse. Return ppm_range and confidence; do not imply measured precision by displaying many decimal places.

hnmr_bins.mult: from neighboring nonequivalent proton sets; n+1 only when applicable
from coupling graph; CH2 hydrogens may need separate treatment
usually singlet when no resolved long-range coupling exists
usually singlet when the methyl is directly bonded to the carbonyl carbon
from adjacent proton sets; include small aldehyde coupling when present
usually singlet under rapid OH exchange; no routine splitting through oxygen
from carbon-attached neighbors, excluding rapidly exchanging OH

hnmr_bins.note: Use instead of adding an unrestricted alcohol shift to an unrestricted carbonyl shift.

hnmr_bins.mult: small coupling to alpha protons; singlet only if unresolved or absent

hnmr_bins.note: Strongly solvent-, concentration-, temperature-, and exchange-dependent.

nmr_environment_rules: A methyl directly attached to C=O is an acyl methyl; a methyl separated from C=O by CH2 is not.
An ester alkoxy O-CH2 is more downfield in 1H than a typical alcohol CH2OH. Neither is an alpha-carbonyl CH2 unless it also has a direct bond to the carbonyl carbon.
For simple vicinal polyols, a small additional 13C deshielding of approximately 3-5 ppm may be used relative to isolated alcohol defaults, with enlarged uncertainty rather than claimed precision.
For atoms beta to O, Br, or C=O, permit a modest class-specific adjustment or wider range. Do not reclassify them as directly attached atoms.
Do not show resolved proton splitting by Br in ordinary teaching 1H spectra; bromine quadrupolar relaxation normally prevents a simple useful H-Br splitting pattern.
An NMR bin listed for an unsupported IR class does not imply that a complete IR template for that class has been calibrated.

checks: Primary OH and split primary C-O cluster; no carbonyl.
1H: 3H triplet, 2H quartet, nominal 1H broad OH singlet.
13C: two environments.
Smooth OH onset, not random structure above 3500.
Primary C-O cluster plus additional eligible chain/coupled modes.
The central CH2 is coupled to distinct CH3 and CH2 sets; an apparent sextet is possible only when the relevant couplings are similar.
13C: three environments.
Secondary C-O cluster and isopropyl methyl-bend pair.
1H: equivalent methyls give a 6H doublet; CH gives a 1H septet; OH is broad by default.
13C: two environments, not three.
Acid canyon, narrow carbonyl core, C-O structure, and approximately 930 acid out-of-plane envelope.
1H: 3H acyl-methyl singlet and broad acid proton.
13C: two environments.
Retain acid diagnostics while replacing alpha-methyl behavior with alpha-CH2 behavior.
1H: terminal 3H triplet, alpha 2H quartet, broad acid proton.
13C: three environments.
Ketone carbonyl, enhanced acyl-methyl bend, no intrinsic OH.
1H: one 6H singlet.
13C: two environments.
Aldehyde carbonyl and explicitly prior-based weak aldehydic CH pair.
1H: CHO may be a small-J triplet; alpha CH2 may be a quartet of doublets; terminal CH3 is a triplet.
13C: three environments.
One broad polyol OH envelope with combined primary and secondary C-O structure.
13C: equivalent terminal carbons plus central carbon give two environments.
Do not assume all four terminal CH2 hydrogens constitute one uncomplicated first-order resonance without stereotopicity and coupling analysis.
Ester carbonyl and differentiated C-O clusters; no intrinsic OH.
1H: acyl CH3 singlet, OCH2 quartet, terminal CH3 triplet.
13C: four environments.
Alkyl pattern, CH2Br deformation, eligible chain rock, and C-Br band; no OH or carbonyl.
13C: four environments, with C-Br assigned separately from ordinary alkyl CH2.
New molecule: combine ester and secondary-alcohol motifs.
Do not generate a carboxylic-acid canyon or acid-dimer band.
Keep methoxy, CHOH, methyl, and carbonyl NMR environments distinct.
New ketone: preserve the ketone band family without copying acetone's complete fingerprint.
1H: acyl CH3 singlet, alpha CH2 quartet, terminal CH3 triplet.
13C: four environments.
Equivalent atom-renumbered or differently written SMILES produce identical ordered band parameters and NMR environment sets.
Adding a functional group changes only its own motifs and chemically connected environment adjustments.
No ring or aromatic molecule reaches the renderer.

do_not: Claim the user-supplied model label verifies the serving model identity.
Memorize or interpolate a named molecule's full polyline.
Treat the supplied kinds metadata as NMR measurements.
Add aromatic out-of-plane bands to an acyclic non-aromatic generator.
Use random jags above 1500 or uniform random noise in the fingerprint region.
Use one Gaussian for all alcohols or copy one fingerprint to all alcohol classes.
Add OH to acetone or ethyl acetate because their traces contain small high-frequency depressions.
Treat the deep approximately 1880 acetic-acid depression as a required acid fundamental; it is not a trustworthy transferable assignment.
Learn a universal alkene-like approximately 3130 band from the saturated propionaldehyde trace.
Force every alcohol to have a carboxylic-acid-like tail to 2500.
Force every ester to reproduce ethyl acetate's exact 939/917 pair.
Force every secondary alcohol to reproduce the exact 954 minimum of 2-propanol.
Make the 1500-500 fingerprint region flat when the graph supplies bends, C-O, C-Br, or skeletal modes.
Populate the fingerprint with strong unassigned peaks merely to make it look experimental.
Double-count an acid OH as an alcohol OH or an ester as both acid and ether templates.
Assign carbonyl class using frequency alone instead of the molecular graph.
Merge NMR environments merely because they share CH3, CH2, C-O, or ppm-bin labels.
Apply n+1 blindly across inequivalent neighbor sets or diastereotopic CH2 systems.
Report precise shifts, intensities, conformer populations, or coupling constants as if measured.
Silently map unsupported acyclic chemistry to a saturated template.
